newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index ends above 6,000 for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index ends above 6,000 for first time.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 6,000 for the first time Monday as investors celebrated moderate economic growth coupled with low inflation -- an ideal recipe for corporate earnings.
The 30-share Dow jumped 40.62 points to 6,010.00 in the first session after Friday's sixth anniversary of the current bull market, which started on Oct. 11, 1990.
Last week, the Dow topped 6,000 several times during trading but did not end above the psychological barrier.

Driven by the sustained economic expansion, low inflation and a perceived lack of attractive options for millions of investors, the market has made climbing 1,000 points the work of months rather than years.
The market, as measured by the Dow, climbed more than 1,000 points between Feb. 23 and Nov. 21 of last year, about 10 months. It took the Dow just shy of 11 months to close above 6,000.

By contrast, it took the Dow about four years to move from 2,000 to 3,000 and then another a similar amount of time to end over 4,000. Of course, 1,000 Dow points are proportionately smaller now than they were then.
Monday's gain, coming after Friday's rise of nearly 48 points on the Dow, pushed the index above the previous record of 5,992.86 set on Oct. 4.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,209 to 1,061 on volume of 321 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index also set a record, closing up 8.09 points at 1,256.36, surpassing Friday's high of 1,248.27.
Analysts said recent economic news, including Friday's report on the Producer Price Index for September, indicated that inflation remained in check, and that was enough to keep investors bullish.
"It's simply momentum carryover from late last week," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson.
On Monday, stocks had no clues from the bond market, which was closed due to the Columbus Day holiday.

"A lot of players are on a long weekend," said Peggy Farley, managing director at Amas Securities. "The folks who are left are pretty bullish. There's a general bullishness in the market, nothing to drive the market down today."
The Dow index marched forward unchecked virtually from the opening bell.
Within one hour of the opening, it sailed past 6,000 and never looked back. At 2 p.m., with the Dow up 50 points, the NYSE clamped curbs on programme trading.

The modest rise of 0.2 percent in wholesale prices in September, which was slightly less than expected, suggested to some analysts that the Consumer Price Index report, due out on Wednesday, will also not rattle the stock market.

Analysts said the Dow's rally through 6,000 would help the market, which has been in a bullish mode after a summer correction of more than 10 percent, but they did not expect a major run-up in days to come.
"I'm one of those people who think that a Dow 6,000 is not that important," Harrington said. "It may turn out to be so after the fact."
Texaco Inc. led a jump in energy stocks as crude oil prices surged, rising 96 cents to a new Post-Gulf War high of $25.62 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Texaco's stock set a 52-week high, closing up 3-5/8 at 101-3/4. Mobil added 1-3/8 to 118-1/2, Royal Dutch ADRs gained 1-3/4 to 164-3/4, Exxon rose 1-1/4 to 87-5/8, and Chevron rose 1-1/8 to 66-7/8.
Oil prices pinched the Dow Jones Transportation index, which ended down 13.42 points at 2,062.47.
Airline stocks were especially hurt, with AMR Corp., parent of American Airlines, off 2-5/8 to 82-3/4, UAL Corp., parent of United Airlines, down 1-1/2 to 43-7/8, and Northwest Air off one to 31-7/8.
Chrysler rose one to 32-3/4 after the carmaker reported strong third quarter profits.

Technology and cyclical stocks also drove the market. Among the big winners, Intel gained 2-1/4 to 107-5/8. After the close, the computer chipmaking giant reported much stronger-than-expected earnings for the latest quarter.
Also, Gateway 2000 was up 3-5/8 to 53-3/8, Dell Computer jumped 4-1/4 to 84-7/8, and Sun Micro added 1-1/2 to 68-3/8.
Thrifty Payless rose three to 21-3/8 after rival drugstore chain Rite Aid announced it was buying Thrifty in a stock swap deal.
Money centre bank stocks were broadly higher, in advance of an earnings report expected Tuesday from Chase Manhattan. which gained one to 82-1/2.
Among consumer non-durable stocks, Gillette was up 1-3/4 to 74-7/8, and Johnson & Johnson rose one to 52-1/2.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.88 points to 703.54. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.08 to 579.33.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.34 to 374.23. The average share was up 14 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,896.575 up 30.298 or 0.44 percent.
